# Owned Native Simscape Replay Boundary

## Scope and Authority

F06d2 (#11942, parent #11921) consumes the separate Tools
`native-state-replay/1.1.0` declaration and verified owned opaque bytes. The
merged Tools PR5471 source is pinned exactly at
`89415ee859d6fcfe3384b95e5a53691e68bf9c1b`. Its complete Git tree is identical
to the `f52a856e0853de6bae6b5ec9bc1bcd7007ab44b0` source used during native
execution; this equivalence is recorded in the receipt. Chapter30 records an
actual R2025b restart diagnostic. The new owned transport has executed the
synthetic diagnostic in R2025b Update 5, including different future forces;
this does not qualify a production golf model.

## Immutable Ownership and Time

`owned_simscape_replay_files` revalidates Tools integrity and required
capabilities, checks the independent producer binding, and freezes model and
opaque operating-point bytes before exposing a temporary native file boundary.
The decoder receives owned files; it must not reopen the caller's model or MAT
paths. Files are cleaned after normal completion or decoder failure. A digest
identifies bytes, not trustworthy serialized executable behavior.

Native input times are the saved snapshot time plus interval-relative input
times, with Tools' interval-precision gate retained. The snapshot is not
retimed. The request records both producer input prehistory and the separate
replay input-file digest: future controls may differ after the saved state.
The complete envelope digest binds the ordered future inputs and policy.

## Supported Input and Numerical Policy

The current file boundary admits one held actuator-force channel, in N, at
`native_force_input` on the diagnostic's declared translational axis. It admits
the externally forced diagnostic mode, adaptive `ode23t`, the explicit native
operating-point initialization policy and the ZOH From Workspace player. This
is a narrow diagnostic interface, not a general production control map.
The axis ID names the force source's scalar input convention; native mechanical
port wiring determines its sign relative to the measured position. Positive
source input and negative sensor displacement are therefore not relabeled as
world-frame force equivalence.
The native consumer verifies actual tolerances, maximum step, block reduction,
simulation mode, input-player settings, conversion settings and physical solver
dialog parameters. Its configuration digest excludes temporary paths. An
explicit simulation compile supplies a separate structural checksum; native
operating-point restoration remains the compatibility authority. The interface,
contents and release mismatch diagnostics must all read back `error`, because
warning-based partial restoration is forbidden.

## Validation and Remaining Gates

The missing-module test failed before implementation. Fifteen synthetic byte
tests now cover caller mutation, absolute-time export, source and binding
mismatch, path traversal, required unavailable capabilities, wrong policy/frame,
tampered inputs or owned payloads, and cleanup after a decoder exception.
An inconsistent external-load declaration also failed before its fix: that
identity must match the exact force CSV that will execute, and additional
contact policy declarations are unsupported. Two additional RED/GREEN cases
reject production driver/iron identifiers on diagnostic bytes: the file boundary
requires the exact fixture ID, diagnostic variant and model version. Focused Ruff and source typing
pass. Synthetic byte payloads are not valid MAT
or SLX files and supply no native physics evidence.

Actual native tests bind the R2025b class, unmodified clock, loaded source bytes,
effective configuration and compatibility before replaying the entire
0.2--0.4 s interval. Same-input position error is $7.46\times10^{-17}$ m;
changed-future position error is $1.28\times10^{-7}$ m, both below the declared
$10^{-5}$ m diagnostic bound. Discrete error is $1.11\times10^{-16}$ against
$10^{-12}$, and force-injection error is zero in both cases. These bounds
describe this fixture and solver, not general production accuracy.

The v5 replay rejects nonfinite or nonscalar saved times, a two-ULP metadata
clock change, absent or mismatched saved provider identity, and a different
loaded SLX path. The authoritative producer and consumer check the loaded
source path; an older two-argument configuration probe does not make that
claim. The provider digest `10d890272361f57152d07e0d71e2e8afaf2034595db106475caa678dd7efad41`
binds the seven executed MATLAB source files. Both v5 request digests and all
native output hashes are recorded in the receipt and the 59-file fleet-local
archive manifest `F06D2_NATIVE_EVIDENCE_ARCHIVE_V5.json`. Its ZIP SHA-256 is
`23f04ada1c235ec50f7af4eae5e9a5876927d9ddc6fa5a6b2f32a945ed4c4ff6`.
The archive includes the executed model and operating point, so keep it in the
restricted fleet workspace; the committed manifest exposes hashes only.

The independent full runs share the original prehistory and each chosen future.
Replay uses only the suffix, with no prehistory integration or clock reset.
Conflicting base/model-workspace sentinels, compile termination, workspace
restoration, configuration drift, wrong request bytes, failure cleanup and
post-execution byte identity are checked. Complete source and output hashes are
recorded in `docs/development/feedback_controls/F06D2_NATIVE_OWNED_RECEIPT.json`.
The seven-file MATLAB provider digest has a bounded scope; it does not attest
every transitive library or qualify the Python runtime. Native
MAT producers must be explicitly trusted; metadata and hashes cannot make an
arbitrary MAT file safe. Production models, all required variants, contact,
muscle physiology, private capture registration and six-engine parity remain
open. Scientific/manual release remains blocked.

Astra review reproduced capture-wall-clock admission and missing full envelope
retention before fixes. Native admission now requires simulation_absolute and
retains the complete validated envelope with its file hash, alongside the
compact request. Loaded-model identity, solver version and declared frame and
contact/load policies survive materialization for actual decoder comparison.

## Reproduction

Use the required R2025b executable and the exact reviewed Tools dependency.
Run `run_native_simscape_restart(producer_dir)` and
`test_native_simscape_execution_binding(producer_dir)` with `scripts/matlab`
on the MATLAB path. Package the immutable files using:

```text
python3 docs/development/feedback_controls/prepare_f06d2_native_fixture.py PRODUCER_DIR OUTPUT.zip
python3 docs/development/feedback_controls/prepare_f06d2_native_fixture.py PRODUCER_DIR CHANGED.zip --changed-future
```

Retain each printed request SHA-256 outside its archive. Extract each archive
to a fresh owned directory and run
`test_owned_native_simscape_replay(owned_dir, request_sha256, producer_dir)`.
The executed MATLAB sources must match the committed receipt's native hashes.
Later Python admission-only guards retain separate unit-test provenance and
reproduce both executed request hashes under the merged Tools dependency.
Any change to the native sources, runtime or executed request bytes requires
fresh native evidence; an old receipt does not qualify changed execution.
